passage: After the Sunday class at the community centre, Aparna stayed on the lobby bench with a blank card from the notice-board tray. Six years since she and her brother Akash last spoke. She wrote three openings and crossed out all of them. The instructor passed with a bunch of keys and asked whether she needed anything; Aparna said, "Just a difficult note." What she finally wrote was: "Akash, it has been too long. I said cruel things about your wedding and never took them back. I am sorry. You do not have to reply. I would like to hear how you are, whenever you want." She did not add a list of who had hurt whom. At the post box outside, her hand paused. Then the card went in.

qa.q: How many years since Aparna and Akash last spoke?
What might Aparna's paused hand at the post box show?
qa.a: Nervousness about reaching out and fear of how Akash will respond, before she decides to go ahead.

qa.q: What in the note leaves Akash room to decide?
qa.a: It says Akash does not have to reply and asks for news only whenever Akash wants.

qa.q: How might Akash feel on receiving the card?
qa.a: He may feel surprised, wary or moved, and the lack of demands lets him respond at his own pace.

grounding: The protagonist reaches out to a sibling after years of silence with a short humble note that owns her part and demands no accounting.
